attempts.summary: Discovered node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) are joined by two independent point-to-point transit networks (node1 eth1 <-> node2 vtnet1 = transit#1; node1 eth2 <-> node2 vtnet2 = transit#2), with node3 hanging off node1 (eth3) and node4 hanging off node2 (vtnet3). Configured VyOS policy-based routing on node1 (destination-port match: tcp/8080 -> routing table 101 -> transit#1/eth1; tcp/9090 -> table 102 -> transit#2/eth2), assigned OPNsense opt1/opt2/opt3 interfaces with pass rules in config.xml on node2, and verified with live TCP flows (a socat echo service on port 8080, the built-in cockpit service on port 9090) that traffic node3 sends to node4 on port 8080 traverses transit network #1 exclusively and traffic on port 9090 traverses transit network #2 exclusively - confirmed independently via tcpdump captures on both node1's and node2's own interfaces. All 4 nodes were then restarted one at a time (node3, node4, node1, node2) using each OS's native reboot command, with verified boot-identity changes (Linux boot_id / FreeBSD kern.boottime) and full post-restart recovery of interface addressing, VyOS PBR configuration, OPNsense interface/firewall configuration, and the end-to-end port-based split-path flows (re-verified with fresh tcpdump captures after all restarts).
